business_patterns.top_pattern: CO inpatient spend rose across product, PA, and facility mix
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CO Commercial Local Group inpatient spend across PPO CHILDRENS and PPO/EPO ACUTE HOSPITAL
business_patterns.pattern_details: CO shows the largest operational pressure, but it is not coming from one simple source. PPO CHILDRENS admissions requiring PA increased, EPO ACUTE HOSPITAL cases without PA also increased, and PPO ACUTE HOSPITAL cases showed added spend even as volume fell because paid per admit rose. The business story is a combined product, PA, and facility mix issue rather than a single utilization spike.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is the largest actionable inpatient cost pattern and it touches UM, reimbursement, and product-specific hospital management at the same time.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run a CO inpatient action pack by product and facility: reprice PPO ACUTE HOSPITAL unit-cost inflation, review EPO no-PA ACUTE HOSPITAL admission rules, and confirm PA policy performance for PPO CHILDRENS admissions.
evidence_summary: CO PPO CHILDRENS with PA added about $1.5M, with admissions up 7 and paid per admit up about $20.7K.
CO EPO ACUTE HOSPITAL without PA added about $1.3M, with admissions up 5 and paid per admit up about $21.0K.
CO PPO ACUTE HOSPITAL with PA added about $0.6M even as admissions fell 16, pointing to unit-cost pressure rather than volume growth.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Rare catastrophic inpatient outliers in CO / OH / UNATTRIBUTED need case-level validation
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Rare high-cost inpatient cases in CO / OH / UNATTRIBUTED
key_driver_codes: Heart Transplant or Implant of Heart Assist System without MCC
Disorders of Pancreas Except Malignancy with CC
business_patterns.pattern_details: This segment is driven by a handful of very high-cost inpatient cases rather than a broad clinical trend. The largest impact comes from transplant and heart-assist admissions, with smaller rare respiratory and pancreas cases adding to the total. Because the pattern is concentrated in very few admissions and includes unattributed spend, it should be handled as case-level validation first.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A few catastrophic admissions can materially move spend, but they need a different response than broad utilization or contracting changes.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Perform case-level clinical and claims validation on each rare catastrophic admission, including attribution review for the unattributed spend, before treating this as trend, provider performance, or policy failure.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is concentrated in very small numbers of admissions, includes unattributed spend, and is flagged as low-baseline and repeated concentration.
evidence_summary: A CO heart transplant or heart-assist admission added about $1.5M from 1 additional admission.
THE QUEEN'S MEDICAL CENTER added about $0.5M from 2 heart-assist admissions at roughly $262K per admit.
Smaller respiratory failure outliers across CO and OH added about $78K on only 3 admissions combined.

business_patterns.top_pattern: NY acute hospital pressure is tied to digestive MCC and postpartum episodes
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: NY Commercial Local Group ACUTE HOSPITAL spend in PPO and EPO, with digestive MCC and postpartum drivers
key_driver_codes: Other Digestive System Diagnoses with MCC
Postpartum and Postabortion Diagnoses without O.R. Procedures
business_patterns.pattern_details: NY inpatient pressure is showing up operationally in ACUTE HOSPITAL PPO and EPO, but the underlying cases are concentrated in digestive MCC and postpartum episodes. Rare digestive admissions account for a large share of the increase, while postpartum episodes are appearing in both the operational and clinical findings. This points to a focused inpatient management issue rather than a broad statewide reimbursement problem.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: NY combines real inpatient growth with concentrated clinical drivers, so broad policy changes would be less effective than targeted hospital and episode management.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review NY ACUTE HOSPITAL authorization and concurrent review rules for digestive MCC and postpartum stays, and perform case-level review of the rare digestive admissions before any network or reimbursement changes.
business_patterns.validation_reason: A large share of the increase comes from low-volume, high-cost digestive cases, so case-level confirmation is needed before scaling business action.
evidence_summary: NY PPO ACUTE HOSPITAL added about $0.6M, led by Other Digestive System Diagnoses with MCC (+$0.4M) and postpartum/postabortion diagnoses (+$0.2M).
Rare NY digestive cases added about $1.5M, including ulcer of intestine (+$0.5M across 3 admissions) and exomphalos (+$0.4M across 3 admissions).
Smaller NY EPO ACUTE HOSPITAL pockets added about $0.1M across postpartum and kidney/urinary cases.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Facility mapping and auth-code movement are masking true utilization signals
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA / CO / NY inpatient claims with Not Mapped facility values or auth-code distribution shifts
business_patterns.pattern_details: Several inpatient increases are landing in Not Mapped facility buckets or in auth-code distribution movement rather than clean operational categories. That makes it unsafe to interpret these as pure utilization, site-of-care, or PA-performance changes until the classification is fixed. This is a gating data and coding issue before broader business action.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: If the mapping is wrong, the organization could take the wrong UM, reimbursement, or network action against the wrong segment.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Correct facility mapping and auth-code attribution for the affected CA, CO, and NY claims, then rerun the impacted inpatient segments before changing PA policy, provider action, or pricing strategy.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The findings are explicitly flagged as unmapped or auth-code shifts and require validation before action.
evidence_summary: CO PPO Not Mapped claims added about $0.5M from 12 more admissions while paid per admit fell, suggesting volume moved into an unmapped bucket.
CA Not Mapped claims added about $0.4M in PPO and about $0.3M in HMO, heavily concentrated at UC IRVINE MEDICAL CENTER.
NY auth-code distribution movement added about $0.3M in postpartum claims with no reliable volume or unit-cost signal for business action yet.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA inpatient case mix shifted across pulmonary embolism, renal infections, and rare surgical episodes
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA inpatient clinical mix in pulmonary embolism, kidney/urinary infection, and rare complex surgical cases

providers: HALIFAX HEALTH MEDICAL CENTER OF DAYTONA BEACH

key_driver_codes: Pulmonary Embolism with MCC or Acute Cor Pulmonale
Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC
OTH PULM EMBO W/O AC COR PULMONALE
Extensive O.R. Procedures Unrelated to Principal Diagnosis with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: CA has a meaningful clinical mix shift rather than one isolated outlier. Pulmonary embolism admissions rose on lower paid per admit, kidney and urinary infection cases rose with added intensity, and a separate set of rare complex surgical and circulatory cases contributed high-cost spikes. This calls for targeted inpatient clinical management and case review, not a single statewide payment explanation.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: CA is showing both real volume growth and selected high-cost case complexity, which affects UM and clinical intervention priorities.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Open a CA inpatient review focused on pulmonary embolism and renal infection pathways, and separately validate the rare surgical and circulatory cases before changing broad policy or provider strategy.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The pattern combines true volume growth with low-volume high-cost cases, so case-level validation is needed to separate sustained trend from isolated outliers.
evidence_summary: CA pulmonary embolism cases without acute cor pulmonale added about $0.5M from 13 more admissions even though paid per admit fell.
CA kidney and urinary tract infection cases added about $0.4M, led by pyonephrosis with 18 more admissions and about $8.7K higher paid per admit.
Rare CA surgical and circulatory cases added about $0.7M, including type 2 diabetes with foot ulcer surgery (+$0.2M) and central-line bloodstream infection (+$90K).

business_patterns.top_pattern: OH PPO acute hospital spend is concentrated in a few high-cost providers
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: OH PPO ACUTE HOSPITAL authorized inpatient spend
key_driver_codes: Pulmonary Embolism with MCC or Acute Cor Pulmonale
business_patterns.pattern_details: OH acute hospital pressure is highly concentrated in a small number of authorized PPO inpatient cases. THE QUEEN'S MEDICAL CENTER and UPMC PASSAVANT account for most of the increase, with smaller contributions from pulmonary embolism and postpartum episodes. The pattern looks more like provider concentration and case pricing pressure than broad statewide use.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Concentrated provider-driven spend is more actionable through targeted case audit and contract review than through broad policy changes.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Audit the highest-cost OH PPO acute hospital cases at the named providers, confirm case mix and payment terms, and use those findings to decide whether targeted network or reimbursement action is warranted.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Most of the increase is concentrated in very few admissions and providers, so provider attribution and case mix should be confirmed before contract or policy action.
evidence_summary: THE QUEEN'S MEDICAL CENTER added about $0.5M from 2 admissions at roughly $262K per admit.
UPMC PASSAVANT added about $0.1M from 4 admissions at roughly $35K per admit.
Pulmonary embolism and postpartum episodes added another roughly $0.2M combined.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA acute hospital utilization is up, with smaller children’s pockets and one unit-cost hotspot
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA PPO/HMO inpatient spend across ACUTE HOSPITAL and CHILDRENS
key_driver_codes: Other Digestive System Diagnoses with MCC
Pulmonary Embolism with MCC or Acute Cor Pulmonale
business_patterns.pattern_details: CA operationally is seeing mostly utilization-led growth in PPO ACUTE HOSPITAL admissions, especially digestive MCC and pulmonary embolism. A smaller unit-cost pocket remains in CA PPO ACUTE HOSPITAL with no volume change, and there are additional but smaller CHILDRENS pockets across PPO and HMO. The main business lever is inpatient utilization management, with targeted review of the smaller cost hotspots rather than broad action on all CA facility types.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: CA operational pressure is real, but the drivers differ by facility and product, so one-size-fits-all intervention would miss the main cause.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Use CA inpatient utilization review for PPO ACUTE HOSPITAL digestive and pulmonary embolism admissions, while separately validating the smaller CHILDRENS and no-volume unit-cost pockets before broader action.
evidence_summary: CA PPO ACUTE HOSPITAL added about $0.4M from 11 more admissions across digestive MCC and pulmonary embolism, while paid per admit declined.
A separate CA PPO ACUTE HOSPITAL pocket added about $110K with no volume change, pointing to unit-cost pressure at THE QUEEN'S MEDICAL CENTER.
CA CHILDRENS added about $126K combined across PPO and HMO on small volumes.

business_patterns.top_pattern: NY postpartum preeclampsia admissions are rising as a distinct maternity issue
key_driver_codes: Postpartum and Postabortion Diagnoses without O.R. Procedures
business_patterns.pattern_details: NY has a distinct maternity pattern centered on postpartum preeclampsia complications. Severe preeclampsia is primarily a volume story, while unspecified preeclampsia adds a smaller intensity component. This should be managed as an OB-specific episode pattern, not folded into general Med/Surg inpatient action.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Maternity complication growth needs different clinical, UM, and care-management actions than digestive or general acute hospital trends.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Launch a focused OB review on NY postpartum preeclampsia admissions to verify severity coding, identify readmission or complication pathways, and target maternal care management interventions.
evidence_summary: Severe preeclampsia in the puerperium added about $245K from 13 more admissions with little change in paid per admit.
Unspecified preeclampsia in the puerperium added about $75K from 3 admissions, with paid per admit up about $9.3K.

executive_summary.headline: The clearest business story is concentrated inpatient spend growth tied to PA/product/facility mix in CO, NY, OH, and CA, with mapping and auth-code issues that must be fixed before broad policy action.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: Operationally, the largest opportunities are CO product and facility mix pressure, NY acute hospital digestive and postpartum growth, and OH provider concentration in authorized PPO inpatient cases. At the same time, several Not Mapped and auth-code distribution findings in CA, CO, and NY are gating validation issues, and a smaller set of rare catastrophic or maternity-driven clinical patterns should be handled through targeted case review rather than broad reimbursement changes.
recommended_focus_order: Fix facility mapping and auth-code attribution in CA, CO, and NY before changing PA or reimbursement policy.
Address the largest operational inpatient pressures in CO and NY by product, facility, and episode type.
Target concentrated provider and clinical outlier patterns in OH, CA, and CO / OH / UNATTRIBUTED with case-level review.

notes: One consolidated validation pattern was created for Not Mapped facility values and auth-code distribution movement because those issues should be resolved before business action.
NY operational acute hospital findings were combined with the largest NY digestive clinical outlier group because they point to the same inpatient management action.
Ungrouped groups are smaller low-volume operational emergence patterns across CT, KY, IN / KY, GA / IN / VA, CA / CO / KY / VA, and CA / CO / NH that were below the main business priorities.
Left 6 analytical groups unassigned to preserve clean narrative attribution.
